decisions.reason: As the umbrella supplement line is strongly related to the firm's existing consumer-health, formulation, quality, and pharmacy-channel knowledge, management would usually keep it and learn from early demand rather than withdraw it quickly.

The skin-and-hair supplement fits the firm's established OTC and pharmacy business well, so its market signals can be absorbed and translated into modest product and marketing adjustments instead of exit.

Joint-health supplements are a nearby extension of the firm's consumer-health portfolio and can be supported with existing development and sales capabilities, though the weaker visibility suggests some rationalization risk.

The mushroom-based immune supplement is the most niche and least robustly supported concept in the supplement group, so limited visible traction makes redeploying resources more likely than continued refinement.

Despite the earlier valsartan-related problem and the weaker fit stated in the prompt, the firm's strong regulatory, analytical, and manufacturing capabilities make remediation and continued commercialization slightly more likely than withdrawal.

The OTC migraine triptan was launched with dedicated visibility and can still draw on the firm's pharmacy-channel, regulatory, and formulation know-how, so management would usually give it more time before discontinuing it.
